pattern_interrupt.evidence: Glance: 'A skin picker?' huge black bold headline (top 20%) over a levitating stack of 6 rings on a stone; callout reads in <1s. Not native UI, polished studio.

problem_awareness.evidence: On-image 'A skin picker?' = micro-callout of a specific behavior/avatar in 3 words; primary text adds 'designed to calm your mind'.

unique_mechanism.evidence: Dotted-leader list: 'Instant anxiety relief / 100% waterproof / Distracts your mind / Lifetime fidget guarantee'; mechanism = spin/fidget implied, not explained.

visual_proof.evidence: Six rings floating vertically as the hero, each with different fidget parts; ring in use is never shown on a hand; result implied.

friction_reduction.evidence: '100% waterproof', 'Lifetime fidget guarantee', navy bar 'FREE SHIPPING OVER £50' = durability + risk reversal on image; copy adds tarnish-free, heat-proof.

cta.evidence: Navy bottom bar 'FREE SHIPPING OVER £50' is the only on-image action cue; copy: 'Shop our fidget ring deal ... this month only'; button Shop Now.

pattern_interrupt_1_5s.rationale: One dominant focal point (headline) + levitating stack; callout lands at first glance. Familiar premium-DTC polish, not an anomaly, so 7.

avatar_congruence.rationale: master_avatar_research.md § Pains: "I walk around with 2-3 manual counters for multiple zikrs and none are waterproof." (Q01) and § Desires: "I want a discrete tool for tasbih which I can have all the time at work." (Q22). A ring worn all day as a quiet habit tool = same driver; her stress-callout becomes our behaviour-callout. Visual world is generic (no people).

adaptability.rationale: Port: 'A skin picker?' -> 'Lose count when the kids interrupt?' (Q29). Port: floating ring stack -> our black + rose gold ring floating over a stone. Port: dotted-leader benefit list -> our REAL facts only (silent tracking, pulse at 33/66/99, prayer alerts, IP67, 60-day trial, free US shipping). Their ratings/'100,000 helped' are dropped.

MK4: headline alone works as a text ad
red_flags: HR1: small brand wordmark above the headline
MR1: list of benefits without a causal mechanism
